records.source: לַמְנַצֵּ֗חַ מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד׃
records.gloss: For the director, a psalm of David,
pieces: For the music director. A psalm of David,

L.1: For the director: a psalm of David,

R.1: For the leader of the music. A song of David.

decisions.choice: The title is verses 1-2
decisions.reason: The Hebrew counts this psalm's long title as two verses, so the verse numbers here are two higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The title continues into verse 2, which says when the psalm was written, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.heading: Create a pure heart in me

records.source: בְּֽבוֹא־אֵ֭לָיו נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֑יא כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־בָּ֝֗א אֶל־בַּת־שָֽׁבַע׃
records.gloss: when came to him Nathan the prophet, as he had gone in to Bathsheba.
pieces: when the prophet Nathan came to him after he had slept with Bathsheba.

L.2: when Nathan the prophet came to him, after he had gone in to Bathsheba.

R.2: It is from the time when the prophet Nathan came to David, after David had slept with Bathsheba.

decisions.choice: The title is verses 1-2
decisions.reason: The Hebrew counts this psalm's long title as two verses, so the verse numbers here are two higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: Nathan and Bathsheba: 2 Samuel 11-12
decisions.reason: David took Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah, and had Uriah killed in battle to hide her pregnancy (2 Samuel 11). The prophet Nathan confronted him with a parable, and David said, "I have sinned against the LORD" (2 Samuel 12:1-13).

decisions.choice: gone in to: had sexual relations with
decisions.reason: To "go in to" a woman is the usual Hebrew way of speaking of sexual union (Genesis 38:16). The title uses the same verb twice: Nathan came to David just as David had come to Bathsheba.

decisions.choice: slept with
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what the idiom means (m3).

decisions.choice: David ... David
decisions.reason: Readable names David where the Hebrew says "him" and "he", and starts a new sentence, since the title of verse 1 ends there.

records.source: חָנֵּ֣נִי אֱלֹהִ֣ים כְּחַסְדֶּ֑ךָ כְּרֹ֥ב רַ֝חֲמֶ֗יךָ מְחֵ֣ה פְשָׁעָֽי׃
records.gloss: Be gracious to me, God, according to your loyal love; according to [the] abundance of your compassions wipe out my transgressions.
pieces: God, be gracious to me in keeping with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love; \q in the fullness of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} compassion, \q wipe away my rebellious acts.

L.3: Be gracious to me, God, according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love; \q according to the abundance of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} compassion, \q wipe out my transgressions.

R.3: God, be kind to me, because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love never ends. \q Your heart is full of tender mercy, \q so wipe out the record of how I rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: loyal love: chesed
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith within a bond, God's commitment to his people (5:8). David appeals to it, not to anything in himself.

decisions.choice: compassion: tender, motherly mercy
decisions.reason: The word (rachamim, plural) is related to the word for the womb: the deep, tender love of a parent for a child (103:13).

decisions.choice: wipe out: erase, as from a written record
decisions.reason: The verb (machah) is used of wiping a name out of a book (Exodus 32:32-33) and of wiping a dish clean (2 Kings 21:13). The same request comes back in verse 11.

decisions.choice: transgressions: acts of rebellion
decisions.reason: Verses 3-4 use three words for wrongdoing, as 32:1-2 does: transgression (pesha'), rebellion against God's rule; iniquity ('awon), crookedness and the guilt it brings; and sin (chatta't), missing the mark.

decisions.choice: rebellious acts
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a plain word for the meaning of pesha' (m4).

decisions.choice: Your heart is full of tender mercy; wipe out the record
alternatives: according to your great compassion, wipe out
decisions.reason: Readable makes "according to" a reason and says what wiping out means (m3).

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.source: הֶ֭רֶב כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי מֵעֲוֺנִ֑י וּֽמֵחַטָּאתִ֥י טַהֲרֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Much wash me from my iniquity, and from my sin cleanse me.
pieces: Scrub me completely clean of my guilt, \q and purify me from my sin.

L.4: Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity, \q and from my sin cleanse me.

R.4: Wash away every bit of the evil I have done. \q Make me clean from my sin.

decisions.choice: much: the form to be read
decisions.reason: The written text has the adverb "greatly" (harbeh); the form to be read is the command "make much" (herev). The words here follow the form to be read; both mean "wash me thoroughly".

decisions.choice: wash: launder, scrub clean
decisions.reason: The verb (kavas) is used for washing clothes by beating and treading them (Exodus 19:10), not for bathing. David asks to be scrubbed like a stained garment.

decisions.choice: cleanse: make clean for worship
decisions.reason: The verb (taher) is the word the priests used when they declared a person clean and fit to come before God again (Leviticus 13:6).

decisions.choice: iniquity: guilt
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, the word ('awon) means the crooked act and the guilt that clings to it.

decisions.choice: guilt
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of 'awon (m4).

records.source: כִּֽי־פְ֭שָׁעַי אֲנִ֣י אֵדָ֑ע וְחַטָּאתִ֖י נֶגְדִּ֣י תָמִֽיד׃
records.gloss: For my transgressions I know, and my sin [is] before me continually.
pieces: I myself know my rebellious acts, \q and my sin is never out of my sight.

L.5: For my transgressions I know, \q and my sin [is] before me continually.

R.5: I know the wrong things I have done. \q I can never stop thinking about my sin.

decisions.choice: I know: I myself admit it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds the pronoun "I" for emphasis. David does not wait to be accused; he owns what he has done.

decisions.choice: before me continually: it is always in view
decisions.reason: His sin stands in front of him and he cannot look away from it, as 38:18 says of pain.

decisions.choice: rebellious acts
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

decisions.choice: I can never stop thinking about my sin
alternatives: my sin is before me continually
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m2).

records.source: לְךָ֤ לְבַדְּךָ֨׀חָטָאתִי֮ וְהָרַ֥ע בְּעֵינֶ֗יךָ עָ֫שִׂ֥יתִי לְ֭מַעַן תִּצְדַּ֥ק בְּדָבְרֶ֗ךָ תִּזְכֶּ֥ה בְשָׁפְטֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Against you, you alone, I have sinned, and the evil in your eyes I have done, so that you are in the right when you speak, pure when you judge.
pieces: I have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone, \q and done what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} see as evil. \q So {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are shown to be right in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sentence \q and pure in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgment.

L.6: Against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone, I have sinned, \q and done what [is] evil in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes, \q so that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are in the right when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} speak, \q [and] pure when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} judge.

R.6: You are the one I have sinned against, only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q I have done what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say is evil. \q So when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} speak against me, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are right. \q When {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} judge me, no one can say {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are wrong.

decisions.choice: against you alone: all sin is finally against God
decisions.reason: David wronged Bathsheba and Uriah, yet he says he has sinned against God alone. Every wrong done to another person breaks God's command and is first an offense against him, as David said to Nathan (2 Samuel 12:13).

decisions.choice: so that: with the result that
decisions.reason: The words (lema'an) usually state a purpose. Here they say what follows from David's confession: it shows that God's verdict on him is just.

decisions.choice: in the right, pure: proved just and without fault
decisions.reason: The first verb (tsadaq) is used of the party a court declares to be in the right; the second (zakah) means to be clean or blameless.

decisions.choice: quoted in Romans 3:4
decisions.reason: Paul quotes the second half of this verse, from the ancient Greek translation, which reads "and prevail when you are judged", to show that God is true even when people are not.

decisions.choice: speak against me ... judge me
decisions.reason: Readable names the one judged, David himself (m1).

records.source: הֵן־בְּעָו֥וֹן חוֹלָ֑לְתִּי וּ֝בְחֵ֗טְא יֶֽחֱמַ֥תְנִי אִמִּֽי׃
records.gloss: Look, in iniquity I was brought forth, and in sin conceived me my mother.
pieces: Indeed, guilt was with me when I was born; \q sin was there when my mother conceived me.

L.7: Look, in iniquity I was brought forth, \q and in sin my mother conceived me.

R.7: The truth is, I have been a sinner for as long as I have lived, \q even before I was born.

decisions.choice: in iniquity, in sin: sin goes back to the start of his life
alternatives: his mother sinned when she conceived him
decisions.reason: David is not saying that conception or birth is sinful, or blaming his mother. He says that his sin is not a single lapse: it reaches back to the very beginning of his life (58:4; Genesis 8:21).

decisions.choice: brought forth: born in labor
decisions.reason: The verb (chul) means to writhe, and in this form to be brought to birth through labor pains.

decisions.choice: Look: a word that calls attention
decisions.reason: The word (hen) points to what follows. Verses 7 and 8 both begin with it, setting David's sinful beginning beside the truth God wants deep within.

decisions.choice: I have been a sinner for as long as I have lived, even before I was born
alternatives: I was born in guilt, and my mother conceived me in sin
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the two pictures (m1) without suggesting that his mother was to blame.

records.source: הֵן־אֱ֭מֶת חָפַ֣צְתָּ בַטֻּח֑וֹת וּ֝בְסָתֻ֗ם חָכְמָ֥ה תוֹדִיעֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Look, truth you desire in the inward parts, and in [the] hidden [part] wisdom you make me know.
pieces: Yet {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} long for truth deep within, \q and in my secret self {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make wisdom known to me.

L.8: Look, truth {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} desire in the inward parts, \q and in the hidden [part] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make me know wisdom.

R.8: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want truth to fill a person all the way through. \q Deep in my heart, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} show me how to be wise.

decisions.choice: inward parts: the hidden inner self
decisions.reason: The word (tuchot) is rare (Job 38:36) and its exact sense is uncertain. It goes with "the hidden part" in the next line: the inmost being that no one else sees.

decisions.choice: truth: what is true and faithful
decisions.reason: The word ('emet) means what is reliable and true. God wants a person to be true inside, not only in outward acts.

decisions.choice: you make me know: a statement
decisions.reason: The verb is in the unfinished form, which can state what God does or ask for it. Read either way, wisdom comes from God into the place where sin had been (verse 7).

decisions.choice: a person all the way through
decisions.reason: Readable says what the inward parts are (m1).

records.source: תְּחַטְּאֵ֣נִי בְאֵז֣וֹב וְאֶטְהָ֑ר תְּ֝כַבְּסֵ֗נִי וּמִשֶּׁ֥לֶג אַלְבִּֽין׃
records.gloss: You will un-sin me with hyssop and I will be clean; you will wash me and more than snow I will be white.
pieces: Take away my sin with hyssop, and I will be pure; \q when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wash me, I will be whiter than snow.

L.9: Purge me of sin with hyssop, and I will be clean; \q wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.

R.9: Take my sin away, as a priest makes someone clean with a hyssop branch. \q Then I will be pure. \q When {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wash me, I will be even whiter than snow.

decisions.choice: hyssop: a plant used for sprinkling in cleansing rites
decisions.reason: Hyssop is a small bushy plant. A bunch of it was dipped in blood or water and used to sprinkle it: at the Passover (Exodus 12:22), to cleanse someone healed of a skin disease (Leviticus 14:4-7), and to cleanse someone who had touched a dead body (Numbers 19:18).

decisions.choice: purge of sin: take the sin away
decisions.reason: The verb is a form of the word "sin" (chata') that means to remove sin, the word used for the cleansing rites in Leviticus 14:49-52 and Numbers 19:19.

decisions.choice: you will cleanse, you will wash: requests
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the unfinished form, "you will cleanse me", but in a prayer they ask for what is wanted, and the next verbs say what will follow.

decisions.choice: whiter than snow
decisions.reason: Compare Isaiah 1:18: sins red as scarlet will be white as snow.

decisions.choice: as a priest makes someone clean with a hyssop branch
decisions.reason: Readable explains what hyssop was used for (m1).

records.source: תַּ֭שְׁמִיעֵנִי שָׂשׂ֣וֹן וְשִׂמְחָ֑ה תָּ֝גֵ֗לְנָה עֲצָמ֥וֹת דִּכִּֽיתָ׃
records.gloss: You will make me hear joy and gladness; may rejoice [the] bones you have crushed.
pieces: Fill my ears with gladness and joy; \q let the bones {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} crushed dance.

L.10: Make me hear joy and gladness; \q let the bones [that] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have crushed rejoice.

R.10: Let me hear happy sounds again. \q You have crushed me, but now let me be glad.

decisions.choice: bones: the whole person
decisions.reason: The bones stand for the whole self, body and spirit (6:3; 35:10). Being crushed is the weight of guilt and of God's judgment that David has felt (32:3-4).

decisions.choice: rejoice: dance for joy
decisions.reason: The verb (gil) is a word for lively, open joy; it may picture going round in a dance.

decisions.choice: you will make me hear: a request
decisions.reason: As in verse 9, the unfinished form asks for what is wanted. Hearing joy may mean hearing God's word of forgiveness, or the sounds of celebration in worship.

decisions.choice: You have crushed me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the bones stand for (m1).

decisions.choice: again
decisions.reason: Readable adds "again": the joy he asks for is joy he once had (verse 14).

records.source: הַסְתֵּ֣ר פָּ֭נֶיךָ מֵחֲטָאָ֑י וְֽכָל־עֲוֺ֖נֹתַ֣י מְחֵֽה׃
records.gloss: Hide your face from my sins, and all my iniquities wipe out.
pieces: Turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face away from my sins, \q and erase all my guilt.

L.11: Hide {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face from my sins, \q and wipe out all my iniquities.

R.11: Do not look at my sins. \q Wipe away every wrong thing I have done.

decisions.choice: hide your face from my sins: stop looking at them
decisions.reason: Elsewhere David begs God not to hide his face from him (13:2; 27:9). Here he asks God to hide his face from his sins: not to keep them in view and hold them against him.

decisions.choice: wipe out: erase
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verse 3. The prayer for cleansing begins and ends with it.

decisions.choice: guilt
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

decisions.choice: Do not look at my sins
alternatives: Hide your face from my sins
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means (m1).

records.source: לֵ֣ב טָ֭הוֹר בְּרָא־לִ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְר֥וּחַ נָ֝כ֗וֹן חַדֵּ֥שׁ בְּקִרְבִּֽי׃
records.gloss: A heart pure create for me, God, and a spirit steadfast renew in my inner [being].
pieces: God, create a pure heart for me, \q and make my spirit new and steady inside me.

L.12: A pure heart create for me, God, \q and a steadfast spirit make new in my inner [being].

R.12: God, give me a pure heart, one that only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can make. \q Make my spirit strong and steady again.

decisions.choice: create: bring something new into being
decisions.reason: The verb (bara') always has God as its subject (Genesis 1:1). David does not ask for his old heart to be mended but for God to make a new one.

decisions.choice: heart, spirit: the inner person
decisions.reason: The heart is the mind and will, where choices are made; the spirit is the inner life and its strength.

decisions.choice: steadfast: firm, settled
decisions.reason: The word (nakhon) means firmly fixed (57:8; 78:37): a spirit that holds steady in loyalty to God.

decisions.choice: a new heart and a new spirit
decisions.reason: Compare Ezekiel 36:26, where God promises his people a new heart and a new spirit.

decisions.choice: one that only you can make
decisions.reason: Readable explains the verb "create" (m1).

records.source: אַל־תַּשְׁלִיכֵ֥נִי מִלְּפָנֶ֑יךָ וְר֥וּחַ קָ֝דְשְׁךָ֗ אַל־תִּקַּ֥ח מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
records.gloss: Do not cast me from before your face, and [the] spirit of your holiness do not take from me.
pieces: Do not drive me away from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence, \q and do not withdraw {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Holy Spirit from me.

L.13: Do not cast me away from before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Holy Spirit do not take from me.

R.13: Do not push me away from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q Please let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Holy Spirit stay with me.

decisions.choice: your holy spirit: God's own Spirit present with David
decisions.reason: Only here and in Isaiah 63 does the Old Testament speak of God's "holy spirit". It is God's own presence and power, given to David when he was anointed king (1 Samuel 16:13). Christian readers hear in it the Holy Spirit of the New Testament, which is why it is capitalized, as "the Spirit of God" is in Genesis 1:2.

decisions.choice: do not take your Spirit: Saul's fate
decisions.reason: When David was anointed, the Spirit of the LORD left Saul (1 Samuel 16:14). David asks not to lose God's Spirit as Saul did.

decisions.choice: from before your face: from your presence
decisions.reason: To be before God's face is to live in his presence and favor (16:11).

decisions.choice: presence (B); away from you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m3).

records.source: הָשִׁ֣יבָה לִּ֭י שְׂשׂ֣וֹן יִשְׁעֶ֑ךָ וְר֖וּחַ נְדִיבָ֣ה תִסְמְכֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Return to me [the] joy of your salvation, and [with] a willing spirit sustain me.
pieces: Give back to me the gladness of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation, \q and keep me steady with a willing spirit.

L.14: Bring back to me the joy of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation, \q and with a willing spirit uphold me.

R.14: Make me glad again that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save me. \q Make me eager to do what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want, and keep me going.

decisions.choice: your salvation: your rescue
decisions.reason: The word (yesha') means rescue and safety that God gives. David had known the joy of it and lost it through his sin.

decisions.choice: willing: generous, freely given
decisions.reason: The word (nediv) describes a person who gives freely and gladly (Exodus 35:5), and so also a noble person. David asks for a spirit that serves God willingly, not by force.

decisions.choice: with a willing spirit sustain me
alternatives: let a willing spirit sustain me
decisions.reason: The spirit may be the means by which God holds David up, or the one who holds him up. The sense is much the same.

decisions.choice: eager to do what you want
decisions.reason: Readable says what a willing spirit is (m2).

records.source: אֲלַמְּדָ֣ה פֹשְׁעִ֣ים דְּרָכֶ֑יךָ וְ֝חַטָּאִ֗ים אֵלֶ֥יךָ יָשֽׁוּבוּ׃
records.gloss: I will teach transgressors your ways, and sinners to you will return.
pieces: I will teach rebels {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} paths, \q and sinners will come home to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.15: I will teach those who transgress {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways, \q and sinners will turn back to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.15: Then I will teach other people who have turned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} how {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want them to live. \q And sinners will come back to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: I will teach: a resolve
decisions.reason: The verb has the form that expresses resolve. Restored, David will pass on what he has learned of God's mercy.

decisions.choice: return: turn back to God, repent
decisions.reason: The verb (shuv) is the word for coming back to God after going astray (Hosea 14).

decisions.choice: your ways: how God acts and how he wants people to live
decisions.reason: God's ways are both his mercy toward sinners and the paths he sets for them (25:4, 8-9).

decisions.choice: Then
decisions.reason: Readable makes the link with verses 12-14 plain: the teaching follows the restoring.

decisions.choice: how you want them to live
decisions.reason: Readable says what the ways are (m3).

records.source: הַצִּ֘ילֵ֤נִי מִדָּמִ֨ים׀אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים אֱלֹהֵ֥י תְּשׁוּעָתִ֑י תְּרַנֵּ֥ן לְ֝שׁוֹנִ֗י צִדְקָתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Deliver me from bloods, God, God of my salvation; will shout for joy my tongue [of] your righteousness.
pieces: Rescue me, God, from the guilt of the blood I have shed, \q God who saves me; \q then my tongue will ring out with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness.

L.16: Rescue me from bloodshed, God, God of my salvation; \q my tongue will shout for joy [at] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness.

R.16: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the God who saves me. \q Do not hold me guilty for the death I caused. \q Then I will sing with joy about how right {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are.

decisions.choice: bloods: the guilt of shedding blood
decisions.reason: The plural "bloods" (damim) means blood that has been shed and the guilt it brings (Deuteronomy 19:10). David had Uriah killed (2 Samuel 11:14-17). Some take it as a plea to be saved from death, the penalty for murder.

decisions.choice: your righteousness: God's faithfulness in doing right and saving
decisions.reason: God's righteousness (tsedaqah) is his doing what is right, which in the Psalms includes rescuing those who turn to him (31:2; 71:2).

decisions.choice: will shout for joy: what follows the rescue
decisions.reason: The second line says what will happen once God answers.

decisions.choice: the death I caused
decisions.reason: Readable names what the bloodshed was (m1).

decisions.choice: how right you are
decisions.reason: Readable puts the noun as a clause (m2).

decisions.choice: then
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark that the praise follows the rescue (m3).

records.source: אֲ֭דֹנָי שְׂפָתַ֣י תִּפְתָּ֑ח וּ֝פִ֗י יַגִּ֥יד תְּהִלָּתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Lord, my lips you will open, and my mouth will declare your praise.
pieces: Lord, open my lips to speak, \q and I will make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise known.

L.17: My Lord, open my lips, \q and my mouth will make known {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise.

R.17: Lord, open my lips so I can speak, \q and I will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} out loud.

decisions.choice: Lord: 'Adonai
decisions.reason: The title 'Adonai means "my Lord", master; it is not the divine name.

decisions.choice: open my lips: let me speak again
decisions.reason: Guilt had shut David's mouth (32:3). Only God's forgiveness can open it, and then it will praise him. The line is a request, though the verb is in the unfinished form.

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: In address, "Lord" carries the sense of "my Lord" ('Adonai); Literal keeps "my".

decisions.choice: I will make known (B); I will praise (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "I" for "my mouth".

records.source: כִּ֤י׀לֹא־תַחְפֹּ֣ץ זֶ֣בַח וְאֶתֵּ֑נָה ע֝וֹלָ֗ה לֹ֣א תִרְצֶֽה׃
records.gloss: For not you desire sacrifice, and I would give [it]; burnt offering not you accept.
pieces: Sacrifice is not what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} desire, or I would offer it; \q a burnt offering does not please {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.18: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not take pleasure in sacrifice, or I would give [it]; \q burnt offering {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not accept.

R.18: Animal sacrifices are not what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want, or I would bring them. \q Burnt offerings do not please {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: you do not desire sacrifice: no offering can pay for this sin
decisions.reason: The Law gave no sacrifice for sin done deliberately, like adultery and murder (Numbers 15:30-31). The psalm does not reject the offerings God commanded (verse 21) but says that they please God only from a broken heart (verse 19; 40:7; 1 Samuel 15:22).

decisions.choice: burnt offering: an animal burned whole on the altar
decisions.reason: In the burnt offering ('olah) the whole animal was burned, given entirely to God (Leviticus 1).

decisions.choice: accept: receive with favor
decisions.reason: The verb (ratsah) is used of God accepting an offering and the person who brings it (Leviticus 1:4).

decisions.choice: Animal sacrifices
decisions.reason: Readable says what was sacrificed.

records.source: זִֽבְחֵ֣י אֱלֹהִים֮ ר֪וּחַ נִשְׁבָּ֫רָ֥ה לֵב־נִשְׁבָּ֥ר וְנִדְכֶּ֑ה אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים לֹ֣א תִבְזֶֽה׃
records.gloss: [The] sacrifices of God [are] a spirit broken; a heart broken and crushed, God, not you will despise.
pieces: The sacrifices that God accepts are a broken spirit. \q A heart that is broken and crushed, \q God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will never reject.

L.19: The sacrifices of God [are] a broken spirit; \q a broken and crushed heart, \q God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not despise.

R.19: The sacrifice God really wants is a humble spirit, \q a person who is truly sorry. \q God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not turn away anyone whose heart is broken and crushed by sorrow for sin.

decisions.choice: the sacrifices of God: the sacrifices God accepts
alternatives: my sacrifice, God, is (with other vowels)
decisions.reason: "Of God" means the sacrifices that God wants and receives. With different vowels and no change to the letters, the words could read "my sacrifice, God, is a broken spirit"; the text as it is read makes good sense.

decisions.choice: broken, crushed: humbled in repentance
decisions.reason: A broken spirit and a crushed heart belong to someone humbled by their sin and sorry for it (34:19; Isaiah 57:15). "Crushed" is the verb of verse 10: the one God has crushed he does not throw away.

decisions.choice: despise: look down on, reject
decisions.reason: The verb (bazah) means to treat as worthless.

decisions.choice: a humble spirit, a person who is truly sorry
decisions.reason: Readable says what a broken spirit is (m2).

decisions.choice: by sorrow for sin
decisions.reason: Readable says what has broken and crushed the heart (m2).

records.source: הֵיטִ֣יבָה בִ֭רְצוֹנְךָ אֶת־צִיּ֑וֹן תִּ֝בְנֶ֗ה חוֹמ֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: Do good in your favor to Zion; may you build [the] walls of Jerusalem.
pieces: In {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} goodwill be kind to Zion, \q and raise up Jerusalem's walls.

L.20: Do good in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} favor to Zion; \q build the walls of Jerusalem.

R.20: Be good to Zion, as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} love to do. \q Build the walls of Jerusalem strong.

decisions.choice: Zion and Jerusalem: a prayer for the city
alternatives: a later addition for the people's worship
decisions.reason: The last two verses turn from David's own sin to the city. David may be praying for the city whose king he is, since his sin could bring harm on his people. Or the lines may have been added when the psalm was sung by the people, at a time when Jerusalem's walls were in ruins (Nehemiah 1:3).

decisions.choice: your favor: your goodwill, what pleases you
decisions.reason: The word (ratson) is God's favor and pleasure; it comes from the verb "accept" in verse 18.

decisions.choice: build: build up, make strong
decisions.reason: The verb (banah) is used both of building and of rebuilding what is broken.

decisions.choice: as you love to do
decisions.reason: Readable puts God's favor as something God delights in (m2).

records.source: אָ֤ז תַּחְפֹּ֣ץ זִבְחֵי־צֶ֭דֶק עוֹלָ֣ה וְכָלִ֑יל אָ֤ז יַעֲל֖וּ עַל־מִזְבַּחֲךָ֣ פָרִֽים׃
records.gloss: Then you will delight [in] sacrifices of righteousness, burnt offering and whole offering; then they will offer up on your altar bulls.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will welcome sacrifices offered in righteousness, burnt offerings and whole offerings; \q then young bulls will be brought up onto {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altar.

L.21: Then {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will delight [in] sacrifices of righteousness, burnt offering and whole offering; \q then they will offer up bulls on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altar.

R.21: Then {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will be glad to accept the right kind of sacrifices, offerings burned whole on the altar. \q Then people will offer bulls on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altar.

decisions.choice: sacrifices of righteousness: right sacrifices
decisions.reason: Sacrifices offered as God commands and from a right heart (4:6; Deuteronomy 33:19). With a broken spirit (verse 19), the offerings God refused in verse 18 now please him.

decisions.choice: burnt offering and whole offering
decisions.reason: Both are offerings burned entirely on the altar ('olah, kalil; Deuteronomy 33:10; 1 Samuel 7:9). Young bulls were the costliest animals offered.

decisions.choice: they will offer up: people will offer
decisions.reason: The subject is not named: the worshipers in general.

decisions.choice: the right kind of sacrifices
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the phrase (m1).
